subtitle: Unlocking the Memory Potential of Pre-trained File Operations for Long-Horizon Tasks via Reinforcement Learning

additional.label: Additional experiments · November 2026
additional.description: Additional results supplied by the authors for the revised manuscript. These are presented separately from the September arXiv release. Raw run receipts were not independently re-verified for this website update.

main.reference: Table 2 (September arXiv v2; Table 1 in the revised manuscript)
main.aggregation: Equal-weight average across four environments; 128 held-out tasks per environment (512 total). Displayed paper values are retained, including averages computed before rounding.

prior.metric: Negative log-likelihood (nats/action token); lower is better
prior.boundary: Frozen Qwen3.5-4B, rounded point estimates. Supports interface familiarity, not a causal attribution to a particular pre-training corpus.

acquisition.metric: Complete designated memory chains (% of episodes)
acquisition.boundary: Excludes mandatory continuation writes. This metric covers designated memory interfaces; it does not cover all native workspace use.
acquisition.definition: Successful store or revision, later retrieval, and later task use.

coding_memory.boundary: Coding-only analysis, different from the pooled training-quarter metric. Chain categories need not be disjoint.

intervention.metric: Success change from intact memory (percentage points)
intervention.boundary: Forked continuations from the same post-reset state, within eligible tasks only. Shuffled donors are within-environment and length-matched. This is a local memory-content intervention, not a whole-distribution effect.

ablation.boundary: The no-gradient condition retains rewards, critic targets and critic learning. The two continuation conditions intervene at different stages.

external.boundary: Benchmark success percentages. Larger frozen models are capability references, not compute-equivalent controls. These outcomes do not isolate a memory-only transfer effect.

constrained.boundary: Frozen Qwen3.5-4B, no RL, the same 512 tasks. Both interfaces use generation-time grammar and argument-schema masks, without post-hoc repair. This is not a comparison of trained policies under an identical compaction mechanism.

transfer.boundary: Task-execution policy stays frozen Qwen3.5-4B; only the memory-writing/reading policy changes. No further training. Sample counts, intervals and significance are not supplied.

long_context.boundary: Same base model, PPO, task rewards and 200-update budget. Context windows and compaction procedures differ. The long-context policy retains native task files but has no dedicated file-memory interface. This is a practical system comparison, not an isolated causal test of memory.

robustness.metric: Average task success (%), mean ± standard deviation
robustness.boundary: Five training runs per method. Error bars show SD, not confidence intervals. Individual run scores were not supplied.

family.boundary: A separately trained Gemma 3 4B policy; not zero-shot transfer of Qwen weights.
